summary: Tested the v0.14.3-beta security-audit fixes on the backend and the frontend. Backend: new suite test_v0143_security_audit.py, 32/32 passed. It covers SEC-001 user update and role permissions (cross-sede, admin on admin/superuser, self-roles, admin cannot assign privileged roles, superadmin can do everything), reset-password and toggle-disabled restrictions, session revocation through token_version (change-password, admin reset, disable/re-enable: old access cookie gets 401 on /auth/me and old refresh cookie gets 401 on /auth/refresh), must_change_password (403 PASSWORD_CHANGE_REQUIRED, /me and /notifiche allowed, works again after the change), CSRF blocking an evil Origin or Referer on POST/PUT/DELETE while same-origin works, separate lockout counters per CF-Connecting-IP (tested on localhost:8001 because Cloudflare rejects that header on the public URL with error 1000), magic-byte checks on /documenti, /rimborsi/{id}/ricevute and /annunci (fake PDF gives 400; a real PDF/PNG/JPG is accepted and the saved extension comes from the content), annunci rejecting javascript: links, CSV/XLSX export showing '=SUM(1) as "'=SUM(1)" while numbers keep their value, PUT on another user's notification leaving it unchanged, and avvisi-sicurezza being superadmin-only. Startup persistence was checked by hand: a test sede and motivo survived a backend restart, and the superadmin password hash stayed the same. Frontend: superadmin dashboard shows the avvisi-sicurezza box (admin does not); rimborsi list and creation, bacheca, documenti, utenti and guide load with no API errors; the admin Utenti page hides edit/reset/toggle for other admins and offers no admin/superuser/superadmin roles; admin password reset and registration approval work in the UI; Bacheca does not render a javascript: link; LegalPage renders [x](javascript:...) with href='#'. ONE BUG: right after logging in, a must_change_password user is NOT sent to /profilo.

critical.endpoint: core/rate_limit.py get_client_ip (login lockout + all slowapi limits)
critical.issue: SECURITY: get_client_ip trusts CF-Connecting-IP and the leftmost X-Forwarded-For value from the client without checking. Reproduced on the public URL: POST /api/auth/login with 'X-Forwarded-For: 7.7.7.7' produced a login_attempts row with identifier '7.7.7.7:<email>'. An attacker can change this header on every request and bypass the 5-attempt lockout, login 10/min, register 3/h and reset 20/h. On a self-hosted deployment (Raspberry Pi/docker, without Cloudflare in front) CF-Connecting-IP can also be forged.

minor.issue: The response body does not include must_change_password (only /auth/me has it). This causes the frontend redirect bug described below.
Admins/cassieri can upload to rimborsi of ANY sede: there is no check that the rimborso belongs to their sede (same cross-sede pattern as SEC-001).
No lower bound on km_andata, costo_autostrada or importo_pasti: negative values are accepted and produce negative amounts.
Old tests are out of date: they expect version 0.11.0-beta and register without privacy_accepted/termini_accepted, so 5 of them fail. These are not regressions.

ui_bugs.issue: After logging in with a temporary password, the user lands on '/' (Dashboard). The must-change banner is missing, the dashboard and contatti calls fail with 403 and the counters show zeros. The redirect to /profilo only happens after a full page load (page.goto / refresh), because AuthContext calls setUser(response.data) with the login response, which has no must_change_password. Fix: add 'must_change_password': bool(user.get('must_change_password')) to user_response in routes/auth.py login, or call /auth/me after login. Once the user is on /profilo: other URLs redirect to /profilo, and changing the password sends the user to /login so they log in again (this works).

issues: rimborso-data-input uses the browser's native type='date' picker instead of the shadcn Calendar

The markdown link check allows protocol-relative URLs ('//evil.example.com' is rendered as is, because the regex accepts anything starting with '/'). Low risk, since only the superadmin can author this content. Use /^(https?:\/\/|mailto:|\/(?!\/))/

action_items: HIGH: return must_change_password in the POST /api/auth/login response (or refresh /auth/me after login) so MainLayout redirects to /profilo straight after login

HIGH: harden get_client_ip. Trust CF-Connecting-IP / X-Forwarded-For only when request.client.host is a configured trusted proxy (e.g. a TRUSTED_PROXIES env var), or take the right-most XFF hop added by your own proxy. Otherwise the lockout and the rate limits can be bypassed by changing the header
MEDIUM: add sede checks for admin/cassiere on rimborso receipt uploads (ricevute, ricevute-multi)
LOW: LegalPage link regex should reject '//' protocol-relative URLs
LOW: update the outdated version/register assertions in test_phase_b_security.py and test_v0141_gridfs_storage.py
critical_code_review_comments: get_client_ip: header-based IP without a trusted-proxy check (see above). This is the most important remaining hole from the audit
csrf_origin_middleware: also uses Referer when Origin is missing (good); requests with no Origin/Referer are allowed by design

users.update_role: the 400 for a privileged role is returned before the target check, which is fine. Superadmin can remove its own superadmin role (there is no guard against the last superadmin demoting itself)
Several notifications and audit records stay after cleanup because the delete_user path removes notifications but not the audit_log (expected)

success_rate.backend: 100% (32/32 new security tests); registration-approval regression suite passing
success_rate.frontend: ~90% (must_change redirect right after login fails; everything else passes)

seed_data_creation: All test data was created directly in Mongo or through the superadmin API and then deleted: test users, TEST_ sedi/annunci/documenti, the 2099 rimborsi, the custom 'cookie' legal doc, the persistence sede/motivo and the login_attempts rows. The superadmin password was not changed (hash unchanged). Older leftover TEST_ annunci/documenti from earlier runs were also removed. Some audit_log entries for deleted test users remain.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/test_v0143_security_audit.py -v. The file creates its own sedi and users (emails must be lowercase). The CF-Connecting-IP test uses http://localhost:8001 because Cloudflare blocks that header on the public URL (error 1000). It sends X-Forwarded-For per session to avoid the login rate limit, which only works because of the reported XFF trust issue; if that gets fixed, the _login helper in the test will need changing. Next: verify the must_change_password redirect straight after the UI login and the get_client_ip hardening.
rca of the issue: must_change redirect: routes/auth.py login builds user_response without must_change_password; AuthContext.login calls setUser(response.data); MainLayout checks user?.must_change_password, which is undefined, so no redirect until a page load calls /auth/me. Repro: reset a user's password as admin, log in with the temp password, and you land on the Dashboard with 403 errors. IP spoofing: get_client_ip returns headers['cf-connecting-ip'] or the first XFF value as sent by the client; the ingress appends the real IP but keeps the client-supplied first value.
